request.reason: Add only the missing repository library-facade path needed by the already authorized composition supervisor entry. crates/cockpit-repository/src/collaboration.rs defines the supervisor APIs, while crates/cockpit-repository/src/lib.rs declares collaboration as a private module and must re-export those APIs for the existing CLI hidden supervisor entry and controlled integration helper. This records the narrow implementation provenance; it changes no acceptance criteria, verification command, policy, resource identity, or historical failure evidence.

changes.value: Implementation provenance for the composition supervisor facade: crates/cockpit-repository/src/collaboration.rs defines run_composition_supervisor_stdio and the controlled supervisor entry APIs; crates/cockpit-repository/src/lib.rs re-exports these APIs from its private collaboration module for the existing CLI internal supervisor entry in crates/cockpit-cli/src/main.rs and the repository integration helper. This explains the single added scope path and makes no claim that release acceptance has passed.

acceptanceCriteria: A1: Preserve the exact original 16 stable-release product paths and stable SemVer 1.0.1 release invariants. The only added product/source/test paths are the declared composition supervisor, attempt/reconciliation, CLI/MCP parity, and deterministic regression paths in Contract.scope; the only added documentation projections are the declared collaboration language contract and scenario matrix pages. No other product/source/test or documentation paths change. The original Work Item, parity, and generated command-reference pages remain protocol projections. Historical v1.0.0 and v1.0.1-rc.2 identities remain separate.

A2: The stable v1.0.1 source and the scoped Linux process-supervision/retry correction have an independent technical review with no blocking product-code findings; attribute that conclusion to its actual reviewer (agent:Raydot), not human:Ray, and bind the review to the exact candidate head.

A3: Before any tag is created, a Runtime-bound release plan consumes fresh evidence for the exact current source/PR, confirms the existing public stable v1.0.0 tag and Release are the selected no-write N-1 reference, confirms the v1.0.1 tag and Release names are unused, records the provider's actual immutability metadata without overstating it, and confirms the existing workflow gates public Release publication on candidate checks.

After normal PR merge and fresh Runtime publication admission only, create the new immutable v1.0.1 tag on the accepted merge commit. The existing workflow must build and pass candidate install/smoke for aarch64-apple-darwin (Homebrew), x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, and staged full N-1 upgrade from stable v1.0.0 must pass on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu before public Release publication. Do not substitute N/A or another predecessor.

After public Release publication, download the official manifest, SHA256SUMS, and Linux x86_64 artifact; verify their identities and digests and pass public install plus N-1 upgrade from v1.0.0 with post-upgrade checks. Preserve any failure and never replace existing immutable assets.

On the local Apple Silicon macOS host, install the published macOS binary at the declared absolute path and update the CLI/MCP executable binding. Verify that official archive/manifest/SHA256SUMS agree, record the actual installed binary SHA-256 and version 1.0.1, confirm CLI absolute path and MCP initialize plus read-only request. Check a local build only for source/provenance/version; do not require its binary hash to equal the official artifact or mutate provider-global identity configuration.

After every release acceptance step succeeds, Runtime admits cleanup and close, and the exact merged PR branch/worktree cleanup plus final lifecycle receipts are recorded. No tag, release, or asset is overwritten or deleted.

Before marking PR #1022 ready or performing its normal merge, GitHub Actions must be fully successful for the exact current PR head after Runtime admits its hosted Work Item verification. This includes all required route, quality, Rust Contract, repository-gate and 13-package coverage, Windows Runtime, and behavioral-oracle checks. Preserve failed attempts; a changed head requires new exact-head CI.

A10: Linux records the process-group leader identity at activation (PID, starttime, PGID, SID) and reconciles only against that generation. Treat the group as exited only after a complete, bounded, repeatable /proc scan finds no members or finds only Z/X members with a stable identical (PID,starttime,PGID) set, a matching leader identity, and an unchanged latest-attempt digest before cleanup. Any non-Z/X member is active. Missing/inconsistent leader identity while members remain, PID reuse, attempt-state change, scan race, proc read/parse/permission failure, or budget exhaustion is unknown and preserves the worktree. Preserve the existing cwd/open-file verifier check; no per-stateDir single-writer assumption; non-Linux behavior is unchanged. Deterministic tests cover zombie-only, mixed zombie/live, live then killed/reaped, injected malformed/unreadable/identity-change/budget cases; the fixture retains zombie state with WNOWAIT and reaps its own child after assertions, never relying on PID 1.

A11: Run the Linux zombie-only process-group regression as an independent acceptance check, separate from the hosted package-coverage check. Preserve its exact command, exit status, candidate head, Contract digest, snapshot digest, and output as separate acceptance evidence. Keep Contract.verification to the single unfiltered command cargo test --locked --workspace; do not place the targeted Cargo test there because the hosted consumer requires a unique complete workspace-test declaration.

A12: Composition attempts distinguish execution outcome from cleanup disposition. The v3 attempt records executionOutcome (passed/failed/unknown), executionEvidenceComplete, backend-tagged supervisorReceipt, and cleanup disposition (cleaned/deferred/retained/failed/unknown). A v3 execution pass is not proof of cleanup or reuse. Strict terminal reuse requires coherent complete execution evidence and verified cleanup. Legacy v1/v2 attempts without ownership and termination proof remain unknown and cannot authorize reuse or retry. Linux receipts bind schema, attemptId, runNonce/generation, owner and supervisor process identities, Linux boot/environment identity, Runtime identity, repository/target/snapshot, command plan, input environment, and ordered execution-record digest. Enforce spawn→ready→durable registration/fsync→release; on revocation or completion stop new spawns, fully reap descendants to waitpid ECHILD, and persist the receipt durably. EOF, leader exit, or heartbeat alone is insufficient. A crash in any phase or concurrent generation change fails closed. Linux-only receipt fields are required only on Linux; non-Linux behavior remains compatible.

A13: A deferred cleanup may permit a fresh retry only when the prior owned tree has reliable termination proof and a bound receipt, current trusted policy and exact command/source binding, current allowed ordinary admission, and concretely safe command side effects. Path location alone never proves isolation. Otherwise, unknown owner/tree/effects/command source, stale binding/generation, or denied admission blocks before spawn. A safe retry uses a second formal run_admitted_composition call to create a fresh attempt, nonce, and worktree; it reuses no prior result and leaves the old deferred directory untouched. Regression coverage must make two consecutive formal calls: the first execution passes with deferred cleanup; the second safe fresh attempt succeeds while the old directory remains.

A14: Use the approved hidden ai-cockpit internal composition supervisor entry in the existing crates/cockpit-cli/src/main.rs; do not add an implicit module or new binary. crates/cockpit-mcp/src/lib.rs must use the exact Runtime helper identity; library tests use a controlled test helper, with no PATH guessing. Every actual verifier spawn still passes through ProcessStartGate; helper IPC errors or admission revocation produce zero verifier spawns. Keep execution, cleanup, projection, and lifecycle state distinct. After composition, a separate current-receipt verify and green preflight remain required before finish.
